title: HelixPath & Redwood: Listing performance, VPC workflows, and UAT playbook
summary: Technical sync to align marketplace listing requirements, VPC onboarding flow, kernel tuning for inference performance, and a UAT playbook for HelixPath's pilot. AE plus SE presented Redwood hosting options and compatibility tradeoffs; customer provided constraints around private peering, KMS, and quantized model performance. Agreed next steps for network diagrams, a short perf benchmark, and a UAT checklist.
topics: VPC peering and private link workflow
Kernel/quantization tuning for on-prem and Dedicated
Autoscaling and burst behavior for reserved pools
Security controls: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts
action_items: Jordan Ellis | Send VPC onboarding checklist, sample network diagram, and marketplace metadata template | 2026-02-18
Priya Kumar | Prepare a 2-run perf benchmark (latency at 512 tokens) and share results | 2026-02-20
HelixPath (Lena) | Share internal firewall rules and preferred egress IP ranges | 2026-02-17
Asha Raman | Provide list of compliance questions (KMS/HSM/retention) to be addressed in security addendum | 2026-02-19
next_steps: Jordan to push marketplace draft to shared drive and ping HelixPath
Schedule 60-min UAT playbook walkthrough next week (Priya + Markus + Asha)
Run initial perf bench with Redwood Dedicated and report 95th percentile latency
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-02-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Kumar (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (HelixPath Head of DevOps), Markus Feng (Platform Eng), Asha Raman (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: All right everyone, thanks for jumping on. Happy Valentine's day, uh, unless that's a bad day for travel, great. I think we have about 55 minutes. Quick agenda — marketplace listing requirements, VPC onboarding flow, perf tuning notes from our runtime team, and then a UAT playbook we want to run through. Priya is going to lead the technical bits. Sound good?

[00:18] Lena: Yep, sounds good. We mostly want to confirm what we need to provide for the marketplace listing and, more importantly, the network setup. We run strict egress and a private peering with our cloud provider so details matter.

[00:30] Priya: Cool. I'll jump in on the listing first, then the VPC workflow, and then kernel/quantization notes. Quick note on naming: for the listing we need a short description, high-level ref arch, supported regions, and whether the integration requires VPC or can be SaaS-only. HelixPath — it sounds like you want a VPC-enabled listing? 

[00:48] Markus: Yes, VPC-only for the pilot. We need the option to never touch public endpoints. So private link or VPC peering, whichever gives us deterministic egress IPs for firewall rules.

[00:59] Priya: Understood. For Redwood Private we support both models — VPC peering and Private Link style endpoints. One caveat: Private Link tends to be simpler for us if you want zero egress, but peering gives you more direct bandwidth. There's a slight difference in the onboarding checklist and the required CIDR allocations.

[01:20] Asha: From a security perspective we need KMS compatibility, key rotation policy, and whether audit logs include per-request model version and token counts. Also retention windows — can we set retention per-customer for logs?

[01:34] Jordan: Great questions. Short answers: KMS yes, we integrate with cloud KMS and HSMs for Private. We can include key rotation details in the security addendum; audit logs include per-request metadata but token counts are approximated in our current implementation, we can show you schema. Retention is configurable depending on whether you're on Hosted or Private — Private gives you full control.

[01:53] Lena: OK. For marketplace listing metadata — do you have a template? We want to include expected throughput and some latency numbers but we don't want to overcommit.

[02:05] Priya: We have a marketplace metadata template, I'll share that. It includes model families, recommended instance sizes, and a sample performance profile. We'll avoid hard SLAs in the listing — put conservative numbers and reference the Dedicated profile for guaranteed throughput.

[02:20] Markus: On the perf side — we've been testing a quantized variant of the open model; our concern is token throughput and cold-start latencies with very long contexts. Any advice on kernel selection or tuning?

[02:33] Priya: Yes — two notes. One, our runtime automatically picks optimized kernels based on model shape and sequence length distribution; however you can influence that by picking a quantization profile and a compiled variant. For long context, kernel fusion and KV-cache sizing matter — we sometimes see 5–10% variance in tail latency depending on the fused attention kernels. Also, if you're on Dedicated with pinned GPUs we can pre-warm KV caches to reduce cold-starts.

[02:58] Jordan: (interjecting) The short practical takeaway: run a small representative workload through our perf harness — Priya will help you run a 2-run benchmark at 128 and 512 tokens so we can show typical 50th and 95th pct. That will go into the listing as an example.

[03:13] Lena: That would be ideal. For the onboarding flow — what's the typical sequence for a VPC peering setup? We need to schedule time with networking and our cloud ops.

[03:24] Priya: Typical sequence: 1) Exchange desired CIDRs and egress ranges; 2) Redwood provisions peering endpoints and publishes the peer info; 3) You accept on your cloud account and we validate routes; 4) We run connectivity checks and sample traffic. For Private Link we create endpoint services and you create the endpoint in your VPC. We'll share a checklist with exact security groups and routes.

[03:46] Markus: How long does that usually take? We're concerned about syncing calendars across teams.

[03:49] Priya: In most cases 2–3 business days of coordination, the actual network cutover is a few hours if both sides pre-configure. If you require dedicated hardware or on-prem boxes it can be longer.

[04:05] Asha: About logging — can we push logs to our SIEM? We want to ingest audit logs into Splunk and have alerts for model-version changes.

[04:12] Jordan: Yes, we support log forwarding to SIEMs and have webhook/streaming options for audit logs. We'll map fields — model_version is included. We'll send the field schema.

[04:24] Lena: Good. Back to perf — you mentioned pre-warming KV cache. Does that require sustained traffic, or can we run a periodic priming job?

[04:33] Priya: You can do a scheduled priming job — e.g., run a few typical prompts hourly to keep warm. For Dedicated we can also keep a small standby pool to avoid cold starts, but that obviously impacts cost. That's part of the cost/latency tradeoff stakeholders often debate.

[04:48] Markus: Speaking of cost, do you have guidance for autoscaling behavior? How fast can we scale to handle bursts if we don't want to over-provision?

[04:56] Priya: For Dedicated we support autoscaling policies with burst capacity. The control plane supports target latency SLOs and will scale up within the pool or fall back to compatible model variants in Hosted mode. We'll share recommended thresholds; typical scale-up is in tens of seconds to a few minutes depending on queued work and model size.

[05:14] Jordan: Note, we can set up canary rollouts for model changes so you can test with a small percentage before flipping traffic.

[05:21] Lena: That's important. For the marketplace listing copy — should we call out the private-only nature of the offering? We also want to ensure customers know there's a UAT playbook.

[05:30] Priya: Yes, call out "VPC-required" for the pilot. We'll add a linked UAT playbook that outlines connectivity tests, perf acceptance criteria, and security checks.

[05:40] Markus: Can you walk through the example UAT steps now? I want to capture the checklist items.

[05:44] Priya: Sure — high level UAT playbook:
  - Network: validate peering, route tables, firewall rules (ping, TLS handshake), egress IPs.
  - Auth: SSO/API key exchange, RBAC mapping, test role-based access to endpoints.
  - Perf: run perf harness at 128 and 512 tokens, capture 50/95/99 latencies and token cost.
  - Failover: simulate node failures, ensure automatic fallback to secondary region or model variant.
  - Security: validate KMS key usage, rotation, and audit log forwarding to SIEM.

[06:20] Asha: For auth — do you support SAML SSO for the console and service principals for APIs? We typically prefer SSO for console ops and fine-grained service principals for automation.

[06:30] Jordan: Yes, SAML SSO and SSO provisioning is supported; service principals and scoped API keys for automation are standard too. We'll document RBAC roles for the listing.

[06:42] Lena: A couple of edge questions — what about locality? We need model inference in the APAC region for some of our customers. Do you support regional deployments for the listing?

[06:52] Priya: We can list supported regions. For Private deployments you can deploy into a customer region. For Hosted/Dedicated we have region options — we'll include the regions in the metadata. If APAC is required for the pilot we can schedule a regional setup but there may be lead time.

[07:05] Markus: Perf tuning: you mentioned kernel selection and fusion. Do you have knobs we can toggle? Or is it mostly automatic?

[07:12] Priya: Mostly automatic; the runtime picks optimized kernels based on the model graph. But we expose a few runtime flags and quantization profiles. For example, one of our tuning knobs is to prefer fused attention kernels vs. more memory-friendly kernels which can change tail latency. We'll show the tuning matrix.

[07:30] Lena: Any known gotchas with quantized variants? Our engineers reported higher hallucination rates with some 4-bit profiles — is that something Redwood has seen?

[07:40] Priya: Yes, quantization can affect generation quality; we tie quantization recommendations to evaluation prompts. For the listing we recommend a tested quantization profile and include a note about recommended eval prompts. If you care about strict fidelity, consider hybrid approaches (float for key layers, quant for others).

[07:57] Jordan: (brief interjection) We'll include a model note in the marketplace entry indicating which quant profiles were used for the published perf numbers.

[08:05] Markus: About the perf harness — what inputs do you need from us? Sample prompts? Tokenization specifics?

[08:13] Priya: Sample prompts that represent your workload, average and peak lengths, and typical concurrency patterns. Also tell us if you use system-level tool-calling or long chat histories so we can simulate KV cache patterns.

[08:27] Lena: We'll provide a small set of prompts and a representative dataset. Also, our CI needs a UAT plan that can be run automatically — do you have a scriptable checklist or playbook we can integrate into our pipeline?

[08:38] Priya: Yes — the UAT playbook is a mix of manual and scriptable steps. We'll provide a runnable checklist: network tests (scriptable), perf harness (scriptable), and manual security verifications. We'll share a Git repo with example scripts.

[08:52] Asha: On compliance: does Redwood provide SOC 2 attestation artifacts? We need to attach them to our vendor risk assessment.

[08:59] Jordan: We have SOC 2 and ISO artifacts available. For Private customers we can provide more detailed artifacts and support an onsite audit if required. We'll route those through the security portal.

[09:10] Markus: Any limitations on model sizes for Dedicated? We're planning to host a 32B parameter model quantized.

[09:18] Priya: Dedicated supports large models, including 32B variants. There are instance type recommendations; some very large models work better on multi-GPU nodes with NVLink. We'll include recommended instance shapes in the listing metadata.

[09:33] Lena: OK that's helpful. For the marketplace listing assets — who will draft the initial copy? Should we do it or will Redwood draft and we review?

[09:41] Jordan: We'll draft the initial listing using the metadata template. We'll include a short ref arch diagram, recommended instance types, a short perf table, and the UAT link. We'll ping you in the shared drive and ask HelixPath to review.

[09:53] Markus: About billing — does the marketplace integration support metered billing or is it a flat commit?

[09:59] Jordan: Marketplace can support both; for pilots we often do metered usage and then move to reserved capacity with a commit if needed. We'll include billing options in the listing copy as examples.

[10:10] Asha: One more security nit: can we require customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest across backups and model artifacts?

[10:18] Priya: For Private yes; for Hosted we can integrate with your cloud KMS if you want to manage keys. Backups and artifacts encryption can be configured.

[10:27] Lena: Great. Anything else on technical risks? What would you call the top three risks for this pilot?

[10:33] Priya: I'd say: 1) network misconfiguration — mitigated by the checklist and prechecks; 2) perf variance for quantized models — mitigated by the perf harness and careful profile selection; 3) onboarding timelines for regional setups if APAC is required — mitigated by early scheduling.

[10:50] Jordan: Good. Let's capture those in the UAT doc and we'll make them explicit acceptance blockers.

[10:56] Priya: Quick note — we sometimes see transcription quirks in these calls, so just to be clear: KV cache is "KV cache", not cash, and quan-tization sometimes gets hyphenated in notes, apologies if transcription scrambles.

[11:10] (laughter) 

[11:15] Lena: Sounds good. Should we pick dates for the perf run and the UAT walkthrough?

[11:19] Jordan: Let's do perf run week of 2/16 — Priya can run it with Markus on 2/18. UAT walkthrough we can schedule for 2/23 for 60 minutes. Does that work for HelixPath?

[11:30] Markus: 2/18 perf run works; 2/23 UAT walkthrough also good.

[11:34] Asha: I'll aim to have compliance questions in by 2/19.

[11:39] Jordan: Perfect. We'll follow up with the checklist and the marketplace draft. Any final questions?

[11:45] Lena: No, thanks. Appreciate the clear plan.

[11:48] Jordan: Great. Recap of action items: Jordan to send VPC checklist and listing template; Priya to run perf harness and share results; HelixPath to share firewall ranges and compliance asks. We'll close loop over CRM-HP-2026-0142. Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and next meeting invite.

[12:05] End of call.
